# Module `qt`

qt - Qt5 Widgets native GUI, wrapped as an opaque-Int surface.

A small, deterministic subset of Qt5 Widgets for native-window programs. The
C++ QApplication/QWidget/QLabel object model stays in the runtime
(`__vyb_qt_*` shims in `runtime/vyb_qt_bridge.cpp`); Vyb sees only Int
handles (qintptr-sized), Int dimensions, Bool/Int status flags, and String
text. String arguments cross as UTF-8 byte buffers; the title/label-text
getters return owned Strings.

Lifecycle: call qt_init() once. QApplication must live on the main thread,
which is where a Vyb program's main runs. Construction needs a Qt platform -
under X11/xcb with a display, offscreen, etc. On a headless box with neither
a QPA platform nor a $DISPLAY the bridge falls back to the `offscreen`
platform so qt_init() stays deterministic; GUI code is still expected to run
where a GUI is available.

There is no callback signal surface yet: the event loop is *polled*. Call
qt_process_events() to pump paint/timer/input events, and arm a polled timer
with qt_set_timer(ms) then check qt_timer_fired() (it clears on read). This
keeps the module deterministic and testable under xvfb/offscreen, and fits
the Int/String FFI the other stdlib modules use.

Everything returns 0 on success and -1 on error (handle lookups fail on a 0/
stale or non-matching handle; operation with no QApplication returns -1),
except the documented deviations: qt_init/qt_active/qt_window_visible/
qt_timer_fired return 1/0 booleans, qt_window_create/qt_label_create return
a fresh Int handle (0 on failure), and qt_window_width/height return the
current size (or -1 on a bad handle).

<a id="sym-qt_wait_event"></a>
### `qt_wait_event` · fn

```
qt_wait_event(timeout<Int>)<Bool> ->
```

UI scheduling barrier: pump the Qt event loop until at least one control event
is queued (true), or `timeout` ms elapse (false). A negative timeout waits until
an event arrives; 0 does a single pump and returns immediately. This is how a
main-thread UI loop blocks *without* busy-spinning while the asyncs pool runs
background work concurrently. After it returns true, drain the queue with
qt_event_handle / qt_event_kind / qt_event_pop. Returns false if the GUI is not
initialized.
